families.title: Request delivery and composite injection coordinates
families.current_scope: Structural query/form/header/cookie/path coordinates are accepted; live composite mutation remains planned.
preserved_requirements: Preserve exact location, type, occurrence and array/composite identity.
Record raw/encoded channel assembly without silently changing authorization.

families.title: Recursive JSON and XML mutation
families.current_scope: Explicit JSON, JSON-in-string and Base64 preparation is accepted; XML selectors and live execution remain planned.
preserved_requirements: Preserve recursive JSON and explicitly selected nested encodings.
Plan finite XML element/attribute names, values, text/tail and repeated selectors.
Keep offline preparation separate from live transmission and retain transformation provenance.

families.title: Discovery, extraction, forms and combinations
families.current_scope: Closed-catalog traversal and captured-source interpretation do not establish general authenticated crawling.
preserved_requirements: Preserve independent expected link/form/request sets.
Bound depth, exclusions, loops, duplicate links and malformed markup.
Treat AJAX events, form controls and stateful browser traffic as explicit supported profiles.

families.title: Supplied authentication and session success
families.current_scope: Session references and prepared journeys do not establish authenticated execution or safe automatic form filling.
preserved_requirements: Classify safe form fields using explicit supplied values.
Distinguish actual session success, false-success login pages, expiry and failure.
Declare supplied auth modes and redact credential/session contents.

families.title: Soft-404 and dynamic error calibration
families.current_scope: Independent dynamic/noise/redirect baseline controls require a bounded native profile.
preserved_requirements: Distinguish soft-404 HTTP 200 from actual resources using bounded baselines.
Retain dynamic-fragment, nonce, status, generic-error and redirect controls.
An unstable or insufficient baseline remains unknown.

families.title: Technology and version observations
families.current_scope: Observed technology and version must remain separate from vulnerability applicability; old signature datasets are not copied.
preserved_requirements: Retain source-attributed application/server technology and observed versions.
Separate observation from affected-product matching and vulnerability applicability.
Do not migrate unreviewed embedded signature or CVE datasets.

families.title: SQL error and boolean differential inference
families.current_scope: The external-provider result canary does not implement native baseline/true/false inference.
preserved_requirements: Preserve baseline/true/false comparison and response-similarity reasoning.
Account for injected-input reflection/removal rather than treating reflected probes as SQL proof.
Distinguish actual query errors from static SQL error pages, fixed queries and equivalent responses.

families.title: Bounded SQL timing inference
families.current_scope: Timing needs a separately selected finite noise/latency profile; a timeout is not proof.
preserved_requirements: Keep timing inference distinct from boolean/error inference.
Use bounded repeated/noise controls, finite request/rate/deadline budgets and supported dialects.
Unrelated latency or timeout alone cannot establish injection.

families.title: Reflected XSS context and filter inference
families.current_scope: Finite provider reflection coverage does not establish native context inference or browser execution.
preserved_requirements: Locate HTML text, tag, attribute, event and script output contexts.
Retain quote/encoding/filter distinctions and independent non-executable controls.
Reflection alone cannot establish executable XSS.

families.title: Browser confirmation and stored XSS correlation
families.current_scope: A separate governed browser-canary profile and exact stored write/read correlation remain required.
preserved_requirements: Require actual governed browser-canary events for browser-confirmed claims.
Bind stored writes, later reads, session and exact current source evidence.
Clean owned stored state on every terminal outcome.

families.title: File inclusion, traversal and resource proof
families.current_scope: Only the exact owned non-secret file-canary profile is accepted; broader path transformations remain planned.
preserved_requirements: Retain prefix/suffix, extension, encoding and path-transformation distinctions.
Require actual owned resource reads and known source content.
Separate missing-resource/error-path hints from confirmed file-boundary behavior.

families.title: Inert upload and returned-resource validation
families.current_scope: Simulation canaries are target contracts; native upload acceptance, retrieval and cleanup remain planned.
preserved_requirements: Keep upload acceptance, returned-resource retrievability and execution distinct.
Use finite inert owned content, generated names and bounded state lifetime.
Clean uploaded state on success, failure, cancellation and timeout.

families.title: HTTP and meta redirect assessment
families.current_scope: Transport redirect refusal is preserved but is not an open-redirect detector.
preserved_requirements: Interpret HTTP Location and meta-refresh destinations under explicit normalization rules.
Distinguish actual destination behavior from body reflection and same-origin restrictions.
Never automatically follow an unapproved destination to establish a positive.

families.title: Header injection and response splitting
families.current_scope: Passive header posture is separate from bounded marker-only injection proof.
preserved_requirements: Keep injected-header and response-splitting observations distinct from passive header posture.
Use marker-only independent framing/response controls.
Do not weaken global transport framing to reproduce an old check.

families.title: Code, command, SSI and historical execution variants
families.current_scope: Owned inert postconditions need explicit profiles; obsolete variants require deliberate defer/retire decisions.
preserved_requirements: Inventory code, OS-command and SSI families separately.
Use finite owned inert postconditions; distinguish result confirmation, suspicion and timing.
Give historical Shellshock and obsolete variants explicit defer/retire decisions.

families.title: XML parser and entity-resolution assessment
families.current_scope: A finite local resolver/canary profile remains planned; parser errors do not establish XXE.
preserved_requirements: Distinguish XML parser errors from actual local entity resolution.
Use a non-sensitive owned canary/resolver and finite document/expansion/output bounds.
Never infer general SSRF or arbitrary file access from the local profile.

families.title: Session, cookie, URL and HTTPS form posture
families.current_scope: Passive observations and any reversible CSRF confirmation require separate evidence; token absence is insufficient.
preserved_requirements: Retain cookie attributes, URL-session and HTTPS-form observations.
Keep posture, authentication success and CSRF confirmation separate.
Any CSRF confirmation requires an explicitly authorized reversible action and observed postcondition.

families.title: Error exposure and bounded hidden resources
families.current_scope: Accepted Git HEAD and Prometheus checks are finite profiles; remaining exposure and hidden-resource inference remain planned.
preserved_requirements: Retain error, stack, SQL and server-information exposure categories.
Bound hidden-resource filename variations and declare dictionary provenance.
Use soft-404 calibration and fixed/decoy controls before reporting exposure.

families.title: Evidence, findings, jobs and deduplication
families.current_scope: Existing shared contracts own modern evidence and lifecycle behavior; old global registries, retries and runtime state are not migrated.
preserved_requirements: Keep raw evidence separate from canonical findings and manual triage.
Retain job, exact invocation, cancellation, failure and partial-result truth.
Reuse modern deduplication and evidence owners instead of old global state or automatic retries.

xss_refinements.requirement: Quote and event-attribute distinctions need independently authored modern contexts.
Tag handling must distinguish actual executable context from reflection.
Comment, iframe, textarea, noscript and plaintext-like contexts need explicit positive/fixed/decoy dispositions.
Redirect, meta and data-scheme contexts require explicit supported delivery decisions.
IE, Firefox, Chrome and Opera historical variants are not assumed to be modern supported profiles.
The 60 rows declare no protection; protected and partially bypassable variants are additional design dimensions.

limits: Historical readiness annotations are documentation facts, not executed results.
Current test references identify existing narrower contracts; they do not establish complete historical coverage.
The 60 case labels do not contain original executable targets or test programs.
Per-case result-bundle comparison, runtime mappings and complete mindmap expansion remain follow-on issue 409 work.
No legacy code, payload collection, runtime state, credentials or historical target address is included.
